themes_detail.label: Graffiti explosion in Flatbush
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged to 97 THIS WEEK—a 1793% spike above the 8-week average of 5.1 per week—suggesting a coordinated tagging campaign or sudden deterioration of enforcement. This is the most statistically anomalous 311 signal in the district (z-score: 13.08).
evidence: 97 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 13.08 indicates extreme statistical deviation
reporting_angles: Interview residents and merchants on specific blocks experiencing heaviest tagging; photograph affected areas
Investigate whether NYPD/Sanitation has deprioritized graffiti removal or whether a single crew is responsible

themes_detail.label: Commercial noise disruption surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints hit 19 THIS WEEK, an 81% spike above the 8-week average of 10.5 per week, indicating emerging restaurant, bar, or construction-related disturbances that warrant immediate investigation.
evidence: 19 commercial noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 10.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Complements existing high baseline of 1,501 residential noise complaints over 90 days
reporting_angles: Map the 19 complaints to identify whether they cluster around a specific venue, construction site, or neighborhood block
Interview residents and businesses about what types of commercial activity are driving complaints (bars, restaurants, late-night delivery, construction hours)

themes_detail.label: Vehicle noise and safety uptick
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints rose to 19 LAST WEEK—a 300% spike above the 8-week average of 4.8 per week—suggesting illegal street racing, modified exhausts, or other dangerous vehicle activity emerging in the neighborhood.
evidence: 19 vehicle noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Correlates with Non-Emergency Police complaints up 236% two weeks ago (13 complaints vs. 3.9 avg)
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD precinct about street racing, modified vehicles, or organized groups operating in CD 309
Speak with residents about specific times/locations where vehicle noise is worst and whether it correlates with nightlife districts or highways

themes_detail.label: Hazardous materials incidents
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous materials complaints spiked to 3 three weeks ago—a 2300% increase above the 8-week average of 0.1 per week (z-score: 8.69)—indicating potential environmental contamination or illegal dumping that may persist despite recent reporting.
evidence: 3 hazardous materials complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Only 351 total DOB filings in last 90 days; no active ULURP applications that might explain industrial activity
reporting_angles: Identify the specific locations of the 3 complaints and determine if they involve the same site or substance
Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection and EPA to determine if any enforcement actions or follow-up occurred

themes_detail.label: Residential waste disposal crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints doubled to 12 LAST WEEK—a 104% spike above the 8-week average of 5.9 per week—suggesting sanitation collection failures or illegal dumping in the district.
evidence: 12 residential disposal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Complements baseline of 732 Unsanitary Condition complaints over 90 days, indicating persistent sanitation challenges
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Sanitation to determine if there are collection route delays, truck breakdowns, or staffing shortages
Interview residents and building managers about specific blocks or waste types causing problems (overflowing bins, illegal dumping)
